answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks using zero-knowledge proofs tied to tamper-resistant tokens like an ivory smartcard with a non-exportable key. Each agent submits a blinded issuer signature and deterministic nullifier to a distributed reef of verifiers, proving unique hardware provenance privately. Attackers thus incur the scarce cost of discrete certified chips instead of spawning hollow software clones. However, real owners can still lease signing access to colluding operators.
